workEn: The Secret History of the Mongols
title: 元朝秘史 §§275–277
titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§275–277: Batu's feast, Güjüg and Qarqasun, and Ögödei's rebuke
part: §§275–277 — Batu's feast, Güjüg and Qarqasun, and Ögödei's rebuke
source: Mongγol-un niγuča tobčiyan (The Secret History of the Mongols), §§275–277, in the Ming Chinese-character phonetic transcription, as edited with a romanized reading by Shiratori Kurakichi 白鳥庫吉, 音訳蒙文元朝秘史 (Tokyo, 1943), itself based on the Ye Dehui 葉德輝 printed edition of 1905/1908; text taken from the Japanese Wikisource transcription, archived and verified against it character for character. Shiratori died in 1942, so the edition was public domain in Japan before the URAA date and was never restored in the United States. Section numbering (§) is the standard citation system. Romanization convention: Shiratori's, kept exactly as he prints it (γ, ġ, ṅ, ž, č, and the raised dot of γ̇). Translations are made fresh from the Mongolian, with the Ming interlinear Chinese glosses as the primary crib. No modern translation was consulted. langCode is null: there is no text-to-speech for Middle Mongol.
about: After the Kibchak campaign Batu sends word to Ögödei that Büri and Güjüg took offence at a feast, rode off in anger and called him and his followers old women. Ögödei, furious, curses Güjüg and Qarqasun and wants them sent to Batu for judgment; the officers plead that a steppe quarrel belongs on the steppe, Ögödei calms, and rebukes Güjüg for how he marched and boasted. He sends Güjüg and Qarqasun to Batu, and Büri to Cha'adai.
draftNote: The Mongol readings follow Shiratori throughout; the English is a first drafting.

Kibčaγčin, the Kipchaks, a people (the form is Kibčaγ̇ + an ending -čin of uncertain force; Ming 種名) [(種名)]
ajan — campaign, expedition (noun; Ming 征進) [征進]
deġere — above, upper (adverb; Ming 上 'above') [上]
Ögödei, a man's name (personal name) [人名]

sentences.l: Batu, Kibčaγčin campaign from-above, Ögödei Qaγan-to envoy-by reporting, coming:
sentences.i: Batu, on the Kibchak campaign, reported to Ögödei Qahan by an envoy, who came with this message:
sentences.n: Deġerēče (Ming 上處 “from above”) is the awkward word: I read Kibčaγčin ajan deġerēče as “from the Kibchak campaign above/away” and take the envoy (elčin-eče, “by envoy”) as the one who “came”. Kibčaγčin is the Kipchaks, with an ending -čin I cannot explain. Qaγan-(n)a: the Ming 行 marks “to” the Qahan. Everything that follows to the closing mark at medetügei is the message Batu sent.

morph.gloss: müṅke — eternal (Ming 長生 'long life') (adjective) [長生]
teṅgeri — Heaven, the sky as a power (noun) [天]
küčü — strength (noun; stem küčün- before a case ending) [氣力]

Meged, a place (place name; Ming 城名) [城名]
Orusud, a people (people name; Ming 種名) [種名]
to plunder, take captive (verb; analysis uncertain) [擄]

sentences.l: "Müṅke teṅgeri-jin küčün-dür qaγan abaγa-jin su-dur Meged balaγasun ebdežü Orusud irgen-i daγ̇uližu
sentences.i: “By the strength of Eternal Heaven and by the fortune of the Qahan, my uncle, we broke the town of Meged and took the Orusud people captive,
sentences.n: Two dative-locatives, küčün-dür and su-dur, are “by strength” and “by fortune” (Ming 氣力裏, 福蔭裏). Qaγan abaγa-jin is “of the uncle Qahan” (Ming 叔叔的): Ögödei is Batu's uncle. Ebdežü and daγ̇uližu are two converbs in a chain, “breaking … taking captive”; daγ̇uli- is uncertain (Ming 擄 “take captive”). Meged is a town (Ming 城名). The opening mark is Shiratori's.

sentences.t: harban nigen qarin irgen-i žüg-tür oroγ̇ulžu

morph.gloss: qarin — nation, division (noun; Ming 邦 'state, nation'; tentative) [邦]
žüg — direction, side (noun; Ming 正 'right, proper') [正]
dative-locative: at, in (front-vowel form after a voiceless consonant)

sentences.l: ten one nations people-(obj) right-direction making-enter,
sentences.i: and we brought the people of eleven nations in, in the proper way,
sentences.n: Harban nigen is “ten-one”, eleven. Qarin I take as “nation” from the Ming 邦 (tentative; elsewhere it is “back, again” or “division”). Žüg-tür (Ming 正行 “in the right direction”) is “in the proper way”. Oroγ̇ulžu = oro- “enter” + causative -γ̇ul- + converb -žu: “making them enter”, bringing them to submission.

sentences.t: altan žiluγ̇a ičun tatažu salulčaqui

morph.gloss: žiluγ̇a — bridle-rein, strap (noun; Ming 牽胷 'breast-strap') [牽胷]
ičun — withdrawing (word uncertain; Ming 退 'retreat, draw back') [退]
to part, separate (verb; stem inferred from the Ming 分離) [分離]

sentences.l: Gold rein withdrawing pulling parting
sentences.i: Drawing back the gold rein (?), for the parting
sentences.n: Hard, and left tentative: altan žiluγ̇a is “gold rein” (žiluγ̇a is “bridle-rein”, Ming 轡繩, in the published parts; here the Ming writes 牽胷 “lead-breast”, so perhaps a breast-strap), ičun (Ming 退) “withdrawing”, tatažu (Ming 扯着) “pulling”, salulčaqui (Ming 分離的) “of parting”. I take it as a ceremonial moment of taking leave before the feast; the exact image is not certain.

sentences.l: feast let-us-hold saying-together, great tent raising, feast-holding-at
sentences.i: we agreed together to hold a feast, and raised a great tent; at the holding of the feast
sentences.n: Qurimlaja is qurim “feast” + -la- + hortative -ja, “let us hold a feast”. Keġeldüžü = keġe- “say” + reciprocal -ldü- + -žü: “saying together”, i.e. agreeing; the speech is not marked. Qurimlaqui-dur is participle + dative-locative, “at the feasting” (Ming 筵席的時).

sentences.t: bi ede bükün köġüd-ün aqaqan boluγsan bolžu nigen qojar ajaγa ötög urida uγ̇uba keġen na-dur Büri, Güjüg, qojar maγ̇uilažu qurim ülü qurimlan morilaγdaba.

morph.gloss: ede — these (plural of ene) (demonstrative pronoun) [這(的每)]
diminutive: rather, somewhat (uncertain; Ming 些 'a little')
ötög — drinking, a drink offered (noun; Ming 喝蓋 'toast') [喝︀蓋]

Büri, a man's name (personal name) [人名]

sentences.l: I these being sons-of elder having-become becoming, one two cup first toast drank saying me-to; Büri Güjüg two being-vexed feast not feasting were-mounted.
sentences.i: I, being the elder among these princes who were there, drank first, a cup or two of the toast, saying so. Büri and Güjüg, the two of them, took offence at me; refusing to feast, they were put on their horses.
sentences.n: Köġüd-ün aqaqan boluγsan: “having become the elder of the sons” (aqa + -qan, Ming 長些 “somewhat elder”, the -qan uncertain). Ötög is the toast (Ming 喝蓋/進酒). Na-dur is “to me” (Ming 我行), the person they were vexed at. Maγ̇uilažu is “being vexed” (Ming 煩惱着). Qurimlan morilaγdaba: the passive of morin “horse” + -la-, “were mounted” (Ming 被上馬子); I take it that they left in anger, and make the English “put on their horses”. Batu speaks throughout. Keġen (Ming 麽道 “saying”) has no clear speaker; I take it with the toast, “saying so”.

sentences.t: Morilažu Büri ügülerün:

morph.gloss: Büri, a man's name (personal name) [人名]

sentences.l: Mounting, Büri saying:
sentences.i: Mounted, Büri said:
sentences.n: Morilažu is the converb of the same verb, “mounting”; ügülerün “saying”. Shiratori supplies no quotation marks for the speeches of Büri, Güjüg and Qarγasun inside Batu's message; the single marks in the English are mine.

sentences.t: Batu sača böġed bolžu urida ker uγ̇uqun büleġe.

morph.gloss: Batu, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
sača — alike, equal (Ming 齊等 'equal, on a par') (uncertain) [齊等]

sentences.l: Batu equal being becoming, first how drinking was.
sentences.i: ‘Batu being our equal, how was it that he drank first?’
sentences.n: Sača (Ming 齊等 “equal, on a par”) is the glossary's “alike”, here “equal”; böġed (Ming 有間 “while being”) is read as the glossary's particle of sequence; uγ̇uqun is the stem uγ̇u- “drink” with an ending I cannot name. Ker büleġe: “how was it?”. The sense is Büri's complaint at Batu drinking the first toast.

morph.gloss: eme — woman, old woman (noun; Ming 婆婆 'old women') [婆婆]
plural (the ending is uncertain; Ming 每)
sačaγ̇u — alike, equally (Ming 齊等) [齊等]

sentences.l: Beard-having old-women equally becoming heel-by pushing instep-by treading said.
sentences.i: ‘The bearded old women are all alike; (let us) push (them) with the heel and trample (them) with the instep,’ he said.
sentences.n: Saqaltan emeged is “bearded old women” (Ming 髯有的婆婆每), an insult; I think it is aimed at Batu and those with him, but the Ming does not say so. Ösügei-jer ... ölmi-(i)jer are “with the heel … with the instep” (Ming 敎腳後根, 敎腳面), -jer read as an instrumental, which is not certain. Tuližu is “pushing” (Ming 推着; earlier parts gloss the stem tuli- “cover”, 葢); gečikileküi (Ming 踐踏) is “trampling”.

morph.gloss: žurγaldaka — (word unread; Ming 柴打咱 'let us beat/bundle brushwood'?) [柴打咱]

sentences.l: Those bow-having old-women-(obj) breasts their žurγaldaka you. We those-(obj) said.
sentences.i: ‘Those old women with bows — their breasts — žurγaldaka. You: we have said it to them.’
sentences.n: Žurγaldaka (Ming 柴打咱 “let us beat/bundle brushwood”?) I cannot read, and leave untranslated. Qortan is qor “bow and arrows” + -tan “having” (Ming 弓箭有的); ebčeġüd is “breasts” (Ming 胷前每); an-u “their”. “You” and the closing clause are as the Ming has them (你, 咱 那的每行 說了有); who “you” is I do not know.

Qarγasun, a man's name (personal name) [人名]

sentences.l: Elžigidei's son Qarγasun saying:
sentences.i: Eljigidei's son Qarqasun said:
sentences.n: Köġün is “son” (Ming 兒子). Qarγasun is the Ming's 人名 only. Elžigidei is the name conventions fix as Eljigedei (Elžigedei) in earlier parts; here Shiratori prints Elžigidei, so I keep Eljigidei.

sentences.l: Wood tail let-us-join, those-(obj) said.
sentences.i: ‘Let us join on a wooden tail,’ he said to them.
sentences.n: Modun seġül (Ming 木尾 “wood tail”) žübčije (Ming 接咱 “let us join on”): I cannot see what the image is (an insult of some kind); the sense is only the Ming's. Teden-i is “those (object)”.

sentences.t: Ba bürün busu heligetü bulγa irgen-dür morilaγ̇uldažu žöbi tabi bolqu bolba. keġežü

morph.gloss: ba — we (first-person plural pronoun; Ming 俺) [俺]

words.reading: 秣舌驪剌兀勒荅周 morilaγ̇uldažu

morph.gloss: žöbi — is it right? (word from žöb 'right'; Ming 是麽) [是麽]
tabi — is it so? (Ming 是麽; the form is uncertain) [是麽]

sentences.l: We being other liver-having revolt people-among having-made-mount, right? so? to-be-done became saying
sentences.i: ‘We, being of another mind (another “liver”), have set the people on horseback in revolt: is it right? is it so? — it has come to be done,’ saying (so),
sentences.n: This sentence is doubtful throughout. Ba is “we” (Ming 俺); helige-tü is “liver-having” (Ming 肝有的), busu helige a different heart; bulγa irgen-dür “among the people, in revolt” with morilaγ̇uldažu, “causing to mount”; žöbi, tabi (both Ming 是麽) are questions; bolqu bolba “it came to be done”. Who says this is not clear; I take it as part of what was said to Batu.

sentences.l: being-when, Büri Güjüg two-to thus having-been-said, counsel without, were-dispersed.
sentences.i: While this went on, the two, Büri and Güjüg, were so told, and without taking counsel they broke up and went their ways.
sentences.n: Büküi-dür “while being”; qojar-a is dative “by/to the two”; keġegdeġed “having been said” (Ming 被說了); eje ügei “without counsel” (Ming 商量無); tarqaγdaba “were scattered” (Ming 散了). Whether they were told by Batu or the others is not said.

sentences.t: Edöġe Qaγan abaγa-jin žarliγ medetügei" keġen öčižü iležüġüi.

morph.gloss: to report, speak to a superior (stem inferred from the Ming 奏) (verb) [奏]
to send (verb; Ming 敎去 "make go") [敎去]

sentences.l: Now Qaγan uncle's decree let-know" saying reporting sent.
sentences.i: “Now let my uncle the Qahan's decree be made known,” so saying, he reported it and sent (the envoy) off.
sentences.n: The closing mark after medetügei closes Batu's message begun at Müṅke. Medetügei (Ming 知者) is “let him know”, the Qahan being asked to pronounce his decree (žarliγ). Iležüġüi is “sent”, with the envoy as the thing sent.

sentences.i: At these words of Batu the Qahan was greatly angered; he would not let Güjüg come into his presence, and said:
sentences.n: Kiliṅlažu is “being angry” (stem from the Ming 怒); aγ̇ulžaγ̇ulun = aγ̇ulža- “have audience” + causative -γ̇ul- + converb: “causing to have audience”, and ülü “not” gives “not admitting Güjüg”. Üge-dür “in the word” (Ming 言語裏).

morph.gloss: dörmegei — lowly one, low-ranking (Ming 下等 'low grade'; not the place-name Dörmegei) (adjective, used as an insult) [下等]
genitive: of (front-vowel form after a vowel)

sentences.l: "Ene dörmegei ken-ü üġes-tür dölüsküžü aqa küġün-i aman düġüren ügülejü"
sentences.i: “This lowly fellow, egged on by whose words, speaks to his elder with his mouth full
sentences.n: Dörmegei here is the Ming's 下等 “low-grade”, an insult, not the place-name of earlier parts. Dölüsküžü is “egged on, joining the din” (Ming 趂閧着; stem inferred). Aman düġüren is “mouth full” (of words); compare the same phrase in the Qahan's later reproach. Shiratori closes the quotation after ügülejü; the speech plainly goes on, and is closed only at medetügei, so in the English I close it there.

sentences.i: Let us post him as a tanma, and make him climb the rammed, steel-hard towns until the nails of his five fingers are worn bare.
sentences.n: Tanma (Ming 官名 “an office”) is left as the garrison force of earlier parts; talbižu is “posting” (as with the scout above). Dabtamal is from dabta- “ram, pound” (Ming 築到的), of walls built of rammed earth; qataṅγu “hard as steel” (Ming 剛硬). Tamutala (Ming 直至盡無) “until bare”.

sentences.l: Beter bad lowly Qarγasun, whom-from learning, our own-kin-to mouth full great word speaking were.
sentences.i: Beter, worthless, lowly Qarqasun: from whom did you learn to speak big words to our own kin with your mouth full?
sentences.n: Beter has no Ming gloss, and I leave it as a word I cannot read (epithet or name); maγ̇ui “bad”, dörmegei “lowly” as above. Ken-e is “to/from whom?”, with eṅgešigežü “learning, taking after” (stem from the Ming 學). Bidan-u uruγ-tur is “among/to our kin” (Ming 親行; uruγ also “descendants”).

sentences.i: Let us send Güjüg and Qarqasun, the two, together. Qarqasun was one to be beheaded.
sentences.n: Ileje is ile- “send” + hortative “let us send” (Ming 敎去咱). Mököriġüldekü (Ming 可斬的 “fit to be cut down”) is mököri- + causative -ġül- + -dekü; the stem and ending are the Ming's sense only, and I render it “to be beheaded”.

sentences.l: Took-sides they-will-say you; Büri-(obj) as-for, if-say, Batu-to say.
sentences.i: ‘He took sides,’ you will say; as for Büri, if you speak, speak to Batu.
sentences.n: The speech after the curse is hard to follow: alaγčilaba (Ming 偏向了 “leaned to one side”) is read as “took sides”, keġekün as “they will say”, ta “you (polite plural)”; the rest is the Ming's order (人名行 有呵 說呵 人名行 說). Who is meant to speak to Batu, and about what, I do not know.

sentences.l: Cha'adai elder-brother-to speaking let-send.
sentences.i: Say it to my elder brother Cha'adai, and let it be sent.
sentences.n: Ügüležü iletügei: “speaking, let (it) be sent”. The Ming glosses iletügei 敎去者 (“let it be sent”), as elsewhere it glosses it like iretügei “let them bring”; the reading is uncertain.

sentences.i: Let my elder brother Cha'adai know,” he said.
sentences.n: The closing mark closes Ögödei's speech begun at Ene dörmegei (see the note at its opening). Medetügei “let him know” (Ming 知者) is Ögödei's way of passing the matter to Cha'adai.

sentences.i: Among the princes Mongqai, and among the officers Alchidai, Qongqortai, Jangi and the other officers, reminded (the Qahan) and reported:
sentences.n: Köġüd-eče and nojad-ača are “from among the princes / the officers” (Ming 大王每處, 官人每處). Teriġüten (Ming 等) is “and the rest”. Duradγan öčirün is “recalling, reporting”. The speech they make runs to bolqu-ju.

sentences.i: “The decree of your father Chinggis Qahan:
sentences.n: Ečige-jin čin-u is “of the father, your” (Ming 父的, 你的), that is, Ögödei's father. The decree itself follows in two parts, with no verb for the introduction; I supply the colon.

sentences.t: keġer-ün üile keġer-e kü nojalaqu büleġe.

to decide, judge (verb; Ming 斷 'decide a case'; perhaps from nojan 'lord') [斷]

sentences.l: steppe-of matter steppe-in just to-decide was.
sentences.i: the business of the open steppe was to be decided on the open steppe,
sentences.n: Keġer-ün üile “the matter of the steppe” (Ming 野外的事), keġer-e “on the steppe” (Ming 野外); kü is the emphatic “just”; nojalaqu (Ming 斷 “decide a case”) a participle from nojala-, which I take from the Ming and perhaps from nojan “lord”.

sentences.t: Ger-ün üile ger-tür kü nojalaqu büleġe.

morph.gloss: dative-locative: at, in (front-vowel form after a voiceless consonant)

sentences.l: house-of matter house-in just to-decide was.
sentences.i: the business of the house was to be decided in the house.
sentences.n: The same pattern; ger-ün üile is “the matter of the house” (Ming 家裏的事), ger-tür “in the house”. Büleġe, “was”, makes both the standing rule of Chinggis.

sentences.t: Qaγan-(n)i sojurγaγ̇asu qaγan Güjüg-tür kiliṅlažu amu.

Güjüg, a man's name (personal name) [人名]

sentences.l: Qaγan-(obj) favour-if, Qaγan Güjüg-at angering is.
sentences.i: If it please the Qahan: the Qahan is angry with Güjüg.
sentences.n: Qaγan-(n)i sojurγaγ̇asu is “if (the Qahan) show favour” (Ming 皇帝行 恩賜呵), a polite opening for a plea; the accusative (n)i on the subject is as in earlier parts. Kiliṅlažu amu is “is angry”; Güjüg-tür is “at Güjüg”.

sentences.t: Keġer-ün üile bijü.

morph.gloss: present or converb ending (as in bijü), is …ing

sentences.l: Steppe-of matter is.
sentences.i: But it is a matter of the steppe.
sentences.n: Keġer-ün üile bijü: “it is a steppe matter”, the plea that the quarrel belongs to the steppe, outside the house.

sentences.i: Would it do to entrust it to Batu, and send them?” So they said, and reported;
sentences.n: Tüšižü is “entrusting” (Ming 委付着); ileġesü “if (one) send(s)” (Ming 去呵); bolqu-ju a question, “will it do?” (Ming 中麽有). Öčiġešü is printed so; it is the conditional of öči- “report”, “when they had reported”. The closing mark is Shiratori's.

sentences.t: ene üge-ji qaγan žöbšijen žaliražu Güjüg-i aγ̇ulžaγ̇ulžu

to approve, assent (verb; Ming 道是 'say it is so') [道是]
to calm down, subside (of anger) (verb; stem inferred from the Ming 怒息 'anger ceased') [怒息]
Güjüg, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
to have an audience, be received (verb) [拜見]

sentences.l: This word-(obj) Qaγan approving, anger-calming, Güjüg-(obj) audience-having-made,
sentences.i: The Qahan agreed to this word, and his anger calmed; he had Güjüg brought into his presence,
sentences.n: Žöbšijen (Ming 道是 “say it is so”) “approving”; žaliražu “calming” (stem from the Ming 怒息 “anger ceased”). Aγ̇ulžaγ̇ulžu is the same verb as in the Qahan's first anger, but here the Qahan does admit him.

sentences.n: Süjü-ġer: “with admonition” (Ming 敎訓), süjü a word I take from the Ming only. Doṅγodurun is “rebuking” (Ming 恠責).

sentences.t: "Ajalažu odorun žaγ̇ura bögsetü küġün-ü bögse in-ü ese hüledebe keġegdemü či.

bögse — rump, buttocks (noun; Ming 臀) [臀]

sentences.l: "Ajalažu odorun žaγ̇ura bögsetü küġün-ü bögse in-ü ese hüledebe keġegdemü you.
sentences.i: “They say that on the road, going on campaign, you did not spare the rump of any man who had a rump.
sentences.n: Ajalažu odorun: “campaigning, when going” (Ming 征進着 去時). Bögse is “rump” (Ming 臀), bögsetü küġün “a man having a rump”, an odd phrase that I think means beating or flogging men on the march, but the Ming gives no more. Ese hüledebe (Ming 不曾留了 “did not keep, spare”) ends in the passive keġegdemü, “it is said (of you)”. Treat the sense as uncertain.

sentences.t: Čerig-ün haran-u čirai quγulžü odba keġegdemü či.

morph.gloss: čirai — face (noun; Ming 顏色 'colour of the face') [顏色]
to break off, humble (verb; Ming 折挫 'break, humble') [折挫]

sentences.l: Army-of men's face humbling went, said-being you.
sentences.i: They say that you went off humiliating the army's men to their faces,
sentences.n: Čerig-ün haran-u čirai: “the faces of the army's men” (Ming 軍的人的顏色), čirai also “colour of the face”; quγulžü (Ming 折挫着) “breaking, humbling”. I give “humiliating … to their faces” for the humbling of their faces. Keġegdemü is the passive as before.

sentences.t: Orusud irgen-i tere čin-u aγ̇ur kiliṅ-dur ajužu oraγdaγsan-a bolγan aqu-ju či.

morph.gloss: či — you, thou (pronoun; stem čin- before a case ending) [你]
aγ̇ur — mortar, pounding-mill (noun; Ming 碓 'treadle pestle-mill') [碓]

words.reading: 斡舌剌黑荅黑撒納 oraγdaγsan-a

morph.gloss: to be cast in, thrown in (verb; Ming 被投入; perhaps from oro- 'enter') [被投入]
particle (uncertain; Ming 麽 marks a question)

sentences.l: you. Orusud people-(obj) that your mill rage-in fearing thrown-in-to making can-it-be, you.
sentences.i: you. Can it be that you made the Orusud people, in fear of that mill-like fury of yours, as ones thrown (in)?
sentences.n: Doubtful: aγ̇ur is “mortar, pounding-mill” (Ming 碓), and I take aγ̇ur kiliṅ as a rage like a mill, but the figure is the Ming's only; oraγdaγsan-a (Ming 被投入行) is “to those thrown in”, from a verb oraγda- I do not know elsewhere, perhaps oro- “enter” in the passive; aqu-ju (Ming 莫不) “can it be?”.

sentences.t: Orusud irgen-i γaγča-γ̇ar oroγ̇uluγsan metü sedkižü omoγ dura barižu aqa küġün- dür daisurγan aisu či.

to make oneself an enemy (verb) [做敵]
ending of uncertain force (participle or converb)
to come (verb, stem; the ending is unclear, the Ming has 來有 'there is coming') [來]

sentences.l: Orusud people-(obj) alone brought-in like thinking, brave heart holding, elder man-to enemy-making came, you.
sentences.i: Thinking that you alone had brought in the Orusud people, you took a bold heart and came as an enemy against your elders, you.
sentences.n: Γaγčaγ̇ar oroγ̇uluγsan metü is “as if brought in by yourself alone”; sedkižü “thinking” (Ming 想着); omoγ dura barižu “taking a bold heart” (Ming 勇猛 心 拿着); aqa küġün-dür daisurγan aisu “came making enemy to the elder man” (stem as in the earlier daisurqan). Aisu is the Ming's 來 “come”, with a doubtful ending.

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan ečige-jin bidan-u žarliγ-tur bi.

bi — is, exists (verb, perhaps a short form of bü-; Ming 有) [有]

sentences.l: Chinggis Qaγan father-of our decree-in is.
sentences.i: In the decree of our father Chinggis Qahan there is (this):
sentences.n: Bidan-u “our” (Ming 俺的), here including Ögödei; žarliγ-tur (Ming 聖旨裏) “in the decree”; bi “is”, the short form of bü-. The decree follows; Shiratori has no mark at its opening, so the single quotation marks in the English are mine.

sentences.t: Olon ajuγ̇uli gün üküġüli keġekü ese-ü büleġe.

morph.gloss: ending of intention (uncertain): so as to, let …
ending of intention (uncertain): so as to, let …

sentences.l: Much making-fear, deep making-die saying not-was?
sentences.i: ‘Make them fear greatly, make them die deep’ — was it not so said?
sentences.n: Olon ajuγ̇uli gün üküġüli: aju- “fear” and ükü- “die” with causative -γ̇u-/-ġü- and an ending -li that I read as “let/so as to” (Ming 敎怕, 敎死 “make afraid, make die”); gün is “deep” (Ming 深); the phrase is the Ming's, and I do not know the Mongol idiom it stands for. Keġekü ese-ü büleġe: “was (it) not said?”.

Kibčaγ̇ — the Kipchaks, a people (people name) [種名]

words.reading: 阿木舌兒里兀勒荅周-者︀ amurliγ̇uldažu-že

glyphs.s: 阿木舌兒里兀勒荅周-者︀

morph.gloss: to be at peace, at rest (verb; stem inferred from the Ming 寗息) [寗息]
particle of exhortation or assent (Ming 者)

sentences.l: Moṅγai, Alčidai, Qoṅγortai, Žaṅgi and-others-to: risen heart-(obj) side companion making, holding-back, boiling pot-(obj) wide ladle making, let-it-be-calmed.
sentences.i: Mongqai, Alchidai, Qongqortai, Jangi and the others: take the heart that has risen up, make it your companion at your side, and hold it back; for the boiling pot make a wide ladle, and let it be calmed.
sentences.n: Ögödei now turns to the officers who pleaded. Žaṅgi-tan-a is Žaṅgi + -tan “and the like” (Ming 等) + dative “to Žaṅgi and the others”. Degdegsen žürügen-i is “the heart that has risen” (Ming 騰起了的 心), derge nökör “a companion at one's side” (Ming 根前 伴當), tödeġežü “checking” (Ming 止當着); the boiling pot (debülküi toγoγ̇an-i) and the wide ladle (delegei šinaγa) are the Ming's images for anger and its cooling. Amurliγ̇uldažu-že is “let it be calmed” (Ming 敎寗息了着罷).

sentences.t: Teli Keġer-ün üile Batu-ji keġeleġei.

morph.gloss: teli — that matter (reading uncertain; sense from the Ming 那事) (noun) [那事]
Batu, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
accusative: marks the object (after a vowel)

sentences.l: That steppe-of matter Batu-(obj) said.
sentences.i: That matter of the steppe has been told to Batu.
sentences.n: Teli is “that matter” (Ming 那事), the sense taken from the Ming; the ending -leġei in keġeleġei (Ming 說來有) is read as a plain past, “was said”, though earlier parts read it as a question.

sentences.t: Güjüg, Qarγasun, qojar-i Batu medetügei" keġežü ilebe.

morph.gloss: Güjüg, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
Qarγasun, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
Batu, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
to send (verb; Ming 敎去 "make go") [敎去]

sentences.l: Güjüg, Qarγasun two-(obj) Batu let-know" saying sent.
sentences.i: Let Batu deal with the two, Güjüg and Qarqasun,” he said, and sent (them) off.
sentences.n: Medetügei is “let him know” (Ming 知者), here “let him take cognizance of, deal with” (compare the Ming's 敎管者 elsewhere). The closing mark closes the speech begun at Ajalažu. Ilebe is “sent” (Ming 敎去了).

sentences.t: "Buri-ji Čaγ̇adai aqa medetügei" keġebe.

morph.gloss: Büri, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
accusative: marks the object (after a vowel)
Čaγ̇adai — Cha'adai, a man's name (personal name) [人名]

sentences.l: "Buri-ji Čaγ̇adai aqa medetügei" keġebe.
sentences.i: “Let my elder brother Cha'adai deal with Büri,” he said.
sentences.n: A second short order: Büri-ji is “Büri (object)”, with Cha'adai as the one to see to him. Cha'adai is named as the one to see to Büri; the Ming gives only “let him know” (知者).
